title: Application Behavior Model
description: Root document for the Application Behavior Model, schema 0.2. Where the 0.1 graph records what was done, this document states what the application DOES: behaviours, the states they move between, and the actors they are available to. Entities live in top-level arrays and reference each other by id. Elements are embedded inside states, and the interactions that were never performed are recorded as state.affordances[] rather than omitted - an absence is not a finding, and a model that only contains what was walked cannot report what was possible.

schema_version.description: Version of the ABM schema this document conforms to. Deliberately not 0.1: a reader must never be able to mistake a behaviour model for a walk record, because the two answer different questions and would validate against the same shape.

entities.description: The things the application moves between states: session, project, cart. An entity is what makes a transition's effects meaningful - without it, 'storage_changed on localStorage.acme-demo-state' is a fact about a key, not about a session. Boundary (P2): the projection declares only what the run's readings show. A walk whose readings never named the things being moved yields an empty list, and that is a statement about the walk and not about the application - a name invented here would be a claim no reading can be checked against.

state_variables.description: The facts that discriminate between sibling states. Every state.identity.dimensions key must be declared here, with a detection that reads an element or a route, so that 'these two states are different' is always backed by something observable.

behaviors.description: What an actor can do, in domain terms. One entry per user-meaningful action, however many DOM steps it takes.

transitions.description: The behaviour graph's edges: one entry per (from_state, behavior, to_state). A set, not a walk - order and purpose live in journeys[].steps[].

apis.description: The calls the run's readings observed. Boundary (P2): an empty list means no reading captured a network entry - the live 0b run has four readings and none of them carries one - and not that the application exposes no API. The walk is what has to change; the projection does not fill the list in from the outside.

journeys.description: Ordered walks over transitions that reach a goal. The model does not require an actor to have asked for one: a run with no stated goal still produces a journey, with goal_stated false, so the order and evidence of what was done are never lost.

observations.description: Raw evidence index. May be kept in a sibling file (e.g. *.observations.json) once it grows large; the file split is not part of the schema.

coverage.description: Optional snapshot of what the model covers at application.version. Useful for spotting unmodelled areas between runs.

warnings.description: Non-fatal issues recorded at generation time: dangling ids, low-confidence objects, ambiguous states.

entity.description: A semantic thing the application holds and moves between states.

name.description: Semantic noun: session, project, cart. This is the name transitions[].effects[].target paths are expected to belong to.

reads.description: Elements or surfaces this entity is read from.

writes.description: Where this entity is persisted, as a semantic path or a storage key (localStorage.acme-demo-state).

stateVariable.description: A fact that separates sibling states which share route, page_type and variant.

name.description: Must match a key used in some state.identity.dimensions.

values.description: Finite domain of the dimension, when it is finite: [empty, populated]. Naming the domain is what lets a test generator enumerate the sibling states instead of only reproducing the one that was walked.

dimension_of.description: States whose identity.dimensions carries this variable.

stateVariableDetection.description: How a test reads this variable. A detection must read an element or a route: a dimension nothing observable reports is not a distinction a test can make, and therefore not a distinction the model is entitled to draw.

element.description: Element the detection reads. Required for every type except route.

route.description: Route the detection reads. Required for type route.

expected.description: The observed value, recorded as observed. Use a semantic word such as populated or empty when the underlying value is incidental.
